mathematical_review: The equal-singleton mass and restriction identities allow zero event mass and extended nonnegative c.
The uniform conditional theorem explicitly requires a finite measure and nonzero event mass; cancellation uses positive finite c and finite event cardinality.
Conditional ordering applies to the actual Poissonized word measure, using equal singleton masses and finite count fibers.
At positive time every count vector has positive probability because every fiber is nonempty and its common word weight is positive.
At zero time nonzero count events and their totalized conditional measures vanish; the zero vector conditions to the empty word.
Reconstruction checks singleton masses, separates the null branch, and remains valid at zero time and for an empty alphabet.
The pinned manuscript motivates only this fixed-time characterization; chronological event times, independent increments, pathwise coupling, and locality remain outside the theorem.
